## The puzzle

```{=html}
<div class="concise-only">
```

The 2026 Iran war drove Brent to $86 in early March — a windfall for Russia. Putin then offered to mediate between Washington and Tehran, and the Dmitriev intel-trade dangled Iran intelligence in exchange for Ukraine sanctions relief. Trump rebuffed both. Russia got the oil revenue and nothing else: no Ukraine concessions, no CRINK-tightening that protected Russia from Western sanctions architecture, no break in Trump's compartmentalization of the two theaters. Did Russia gain or lose? The answer differs by dimension.

```{=html}
</div>
<div class="deep-only">
```

In March 2026 the Iran-war Brent spike pushed Russian oil revenue to $19 billion for the month, a 95% month-over-month jump. Putin moved to convert the war into Ukraine-relevant gains. He offered to mediate between Washington and Tehran. The Dmitriev intel-trade dangled Russian Iran intelligence in exchange for Ukraine sanctions relief. Both offers were rebuffed by Trump. Russia's compartmentalization-breaking attempt failed. The structural reason: Russia's multi-front military incapacity (refining output at 4.69 mb/d in May, a 15-year low; 5 straight months casualties exceeding recruitment) meant Russia could not credibly threaten escalation linkage; and the CRINK coalition (China-Russia-Iran-North Korea) is structurally loose-coupled, with no senior partner able to deliver concessions. Meanwhile Ukraine converted Iran-war demand into 201 deployed defense specialists across 5 Gulf states and 10-year defense cooperation frameworks with Saudi/Qatar/UAE (Haavik / Security Distillery, April 20). Russia's gains are *passive* (oil revenue dependent on price and Strait conditions; March federal budget short 234.3B rubles despite the windfall). Ukraine's gains are *active* (defense partnerships scaled to $50B/year production; export permits; deployed specialists). On a 12-month horizon, the trajectory is asymmetric and time-decaying. The puzzle Q7 sets: what does the Iran war mean for the Russia-Ukraine war?

Russia attempted to break Trump's compartmentalization (Putin mediation, Dmitriev intel-trade) and was rebuffed. ## Methodology — principled-multi-framework finding (META rule 7 application)

This chapter applies the standard 8-step protocol. The devil's-advocate pass (12 critiques + Critique 6.5) was the most aggressive of the project, producing substantial revisions. Two were structurally critical: (1) DA Critique 6 forced explicit specification of a 12-month forecast horizon — longer horizons depend on Western-support-fragility (reversible-on-one-election) and are downgraded to "currently-dominant 12-month pattern." (2) DA Critique 2 was accepted: the ω cop-out (Goemans vs Reiter/Fearon framework indeterminacy) was resolved toward Goemans, P(Goemans within) ≈ 0.60. Headline posterior lowered from 0.50 to 0.45 to acknowledge T3-inflation but framework structure preserved. META rule 7 applies: each of the four framework families is pre-analysis-domain-distinct in the IR literature (battlefield vs economic vs coalition vs bargaining), in the same way Q9's Pape/Posen/Ikenberry/Farrell-Newman are domain-distinct.
:::

::: {focus-on="cr-stage1"}
[**Four framework-domains in the IR literature.** Q7 asks the same question through four lenses: battlefield ([Mearsheimer / Posen / Biddle]{.gloss data-gloss="mearsheimer-attrition"}); economic / petrostate ([Colgan / Ross / Drezner]{.gloss data-gloss="colgan-petrostate"}); coalition ([Pressman / Lake / Farrell-Newman]{.gloss data-gloss="pressman-alliance-restraint"}); bargaining / war-termination ([Goemans / Reiter / Fearon]{.gloss data-gloss="goemans-gamble-resurrection"}). Each family is domain-distinct prior to application; the dimension-specific finding is principled multi-framework.]{.concise-only}

::: {.deep-only}
**Four framework-domains in the IR literature, each pre-analysis-domain-distinct.** *Battlefield / operational:* [Mearsheimer 1983]{.gloss data-gloss="mearsheimer-attrition"} on blitzkrieg-vs-attrition deterrence; Posen 1984 on doctrine adaptation under multi-front pressure; Biddle 2004 on combined-arms execution. The literature does not extend naturally to economic or coalition domains. *Economic / petrostate / sanctions:* [Colgan 2013]{.gloss data-gloss="colgan-petrostate"} on revolutionary-vs-non-revolutionary petrostate aggression; Ross 2012 on oil-revenue volatility; [Drezner 1999/2025]{.gloss data-gloss="drezner-sanctions"} on sanctions effectiveness vs ineffectiveness. The literature does not extend to battlefield doctrine or coalition restraint. *Coalition / alliance-restraint / interdependence:* [Pressman 2008]{.gloss data-gloss="pressman-alliance-restraint"} on alliance-restraint of the junior partner; Lake 2009 on hierarchy; [Farrell-Newman 2019]{.gloss data-gloss="farrell-newman-interdependence"} on weaponized interdependence. The literature does not extend to battlefield doctrine or petrostate political-economy. *Bargaining / war-termination:* [Goemans 2000]{.gloss data-gloss="goemans-gamble-resurrection"} on gamble-for-resurrection in mixed regimes; Reiter 2009 on information-driven settlement willingness; Fearon 1996 / Powell 2006 on dynamic bargaining + commitment problems. The literature does not extend to operational battlefield or petrostate aggression. Each family's domain is specified in the literature before being applied to Russia-Ukraine. The dimension-specific finding is therefore principled multi-framework — META rule 7 cleared.
:::
:::

::: {focus-on="cr-stage2"}
[**τ — Asymmetric trajectory** (load-bearing P ≈ 0.65). Two sub-channels. *τ-military:* Russia's refining output dropped to 4.69 mb/d (15-year low); 5 straight months casualties greater than recruitment; first net territory loss since August 2024. *τ-economic-coalition:* Russia's March $19B oil revenue offset by 234.3B-ruble budget shortfall and $60B Q1 deficit; Ukraine's 201 deployed specialists + 10-year defense frameworks with Saudi/Qatar/UAE compound across 12 months.]{.concise-only}

::: {.deep-only}
**τ — Asymmetric Russia-degrades-Ukraine-compounds trajectory** (P load-bearing ≈ 0.65). Two sub-channels operating together. *τ-military:* Russia is constrained by Ukrainian defense-dominant attrition (Mearsheimer-Posen multi-front constraint applied to ongoing-war timescales). Ukraine actively degrades Russian war-economy chokepoints via deep-strike — Pape's coercion-doctrine inverted: Ukraine doing strategic-strike-for-coercion against Russia's refining, C4ISR feedstock, and storage infrastructure. Empirical anchors: Russian refining output fell to 4.69 mb/d in May 2026 (a 15-year low, with ~20% of capacity destroyed); Russian daily territorial advance rate fell from 9.76 to 2.9 km²/day; the first net territory loss since August 2024 (-116 km², April 2026, per ISW 2 May); the Cheboksary 5 May strike on VNIIR-Progress C4ISR feedstock production using Flamingo missiles at >1,500 km range. *τ-economic-coalition:* Russia's gains are passive — oil revenue dependent on price and Strait conditions, with March $19B (+95% MoM) offset by fuel-support payments to refiners (15B → 207.5B rubles), a March federal budget shortfall of 234.3B rubles despite the windfall, and Q1 2026 federal deficit reaching ~$60B (4.6 trillion rubles, exceeding the full-year 3.8 trillion target). Russia's passive gains evaporate. Ukraine's gains are active — defense partnerships with Saudi/Qatar/UAE, production base scaled to $50B/year, 201 deployed specialists across 5 Gulf states (Haavik / Security Distillery 20 April, T3 single-sourced), 10-year defense cooperation frameworks. Ukraine's active gains compound across the 12-month horizon. The sub-channel collapse (σ + π → τ) was retained on causal grounds against DA Critique 10: Russia's military degradation enables Ukraine's deep-strike effectiveness which enables Ukraine's economic-coalition gains — they are causally linked, not coincidental.
:::
:::

::: {focus-on="cr-stage3"}
[**ω*** **— [Goemans-favored bargaining]{.gloss data-gloss="goemans-gamble-resurrection"}** (load-bearing P ≈ 0.55). Five empirical signals all consistent with Putin's gamble-for-resurrection. Putin will continue rather than concede, regardless of objective war-capacity decline. The framework dominates the Reiter/Fearon settlement-pressure prediction.]{.concise-only}

::: {.deep-only}
**ω* — [Goemans-favored bargaining trajectory]{.gloss data-gloss="goemans-gamble-resurrection"}** (P load-bearing ≈ 0.55; P(Goemans within ω*) ≈ 0.60; P(Reiter/Fearon operative) ≈ 0.30; P(other settlement path) ≈ 0.10). Putin's regime-survival concerns push toward gamble-for-resurrection rather than Reiter/Fearon concession-pressure. Goemans's framework predicts that mixed-regime leaders facing personal-political destruction prefer escalation over a moderately bad settlement, even when objective war prospects worsen. The framework predicts continued war-prosecution past the point objective interests would dictate concession. Empirical signals all converging: Levada approval down 11 points to 69%; Victory Day parade truncation (no military equipment displayed for the first time since 2007, attributed to deep-strike vulnerability); Ushakov's "no point in talks" hard-line rejection of negotiations; five straight months of casualties exceeding recruitment (33,200 vs 27,400 in December 2025; pattern continuing through April); the Newsweek "running out of cards" framing; doubled glide-bomb output as offensive doubling-down rather than reduction. These signals are *both* causes of regime-survival anxiety and consequences of war-trajectory deterioration — a Goemans-dynamic feedback loop. **Critical implication**: ω* is consistent with τ. Russia continues fighting (Goemans) while Russia loses ground (τ-military) and accumulates passive gains that decay (τ-economic-coalition). The two mechanisms together predict continued Russian war-prosecution at attrition costs that exceed Russian gains, producing net Russian deterioration despite continued resource expenditure.
:::

### Figure 3 — Pre-registered falsification criteria

The synthesis is testable on three time horizons.

**Near-term (3-6 months, fires by 2026-08-10):**

| Test | Predicts | Falsifies if |
|---|---|---|
| Trump-Xi summit (May 14-15) Russia content | No Russia deliverable | Summit produces Russia-related triangulation language |
| CRINK γ' trigger | No extension to Russia-buyers by end-Q3 2026 | Blocking statute extended to Indian/Turkish/UAE intermediaries |
| Russian advance rate | No recovery >9.76 km²/day sustained | Russia recaptures territory at >9.76 km²/day for >4 weeks |
| ω* commit-Goemans | No substantial Putin concessions at next negotiating round | Putin accepts substantial territorial concession |

**Medium-term (6-12 months, falsifies through 2027-04):**

| Test | Predicts | Falsifies if |
|---|---|---|
| Haavik corroboration | "201 specialists / 10-year frameworks" corroborated by independent source | Single-source remains; downgrade π active-side strength |
| Western support-cut threshold | US/EU weapons supply sustains | US/EU cut by >50% from current pace |
| Oil price sustained-test | Brent/Urals do not sustain >$80/bbl 12+ months | Sustained >$80/bbl for 12+ months |

**Long-term (beyond 12 months — undetermined):** The synthesis *explicitly* does not pre-register long-horizon falsification criteria. On 2027-28+ horizons, the Russia-vs-Ukraine trajectory depends critically on Western-support-fragility (reversible-on-one-election), which is downgraded to "currently-dominant 12-month pattern."

### Figure 4 — Source-confidence tier audit

Of the synthesis's load-bearing claims:

- **[T1]{.tier .tier-1} multi-source verified:** Russia first net territory loss since Aug 2024 (-116 km², April 2026) — ISW May 2; Russian refinery output 4.69 mb/d May 2026 (15-year low, ~20% capacity destroyed) — ISW May 1 + Bloomberg/Argus; March 2026 Russian oil revenue $19B (+95% MoM) — Russian MoF; March federal budget short 234.3B rubles despite windfall — Russian MoF; Q1 2026 federal deficit ~$60B (4.6 trillion rubles, exceeds full-year 3.8 trillion target) — Russian MoF via Moscow Times May 6; Putin Dmitriev intel-trade offer rejected by Trump — Moscow Times March 20; China May 2 blocking statute over teapot refineries (25% of Chinese refining capacity) — Bloomberg + Al Jazeera May 3.

- **[T2]{.tier .tier-2} single-source named:** Russian daily advance rate fell 9.76 → 2.9 km²/day — ISW (computed); Russian crude exports collapsed Mar 25–Apr 11 to 3.5 mb/d (vs Q1 5.2) — Bloomberg/Argus shipping data; Fuel-price-support to refiners surged 15B → 207.5B rubles — Moscow Times May 6; December 2025 first month casualties > recruitment (33,200 vs 27,400) — Kyiv Independent + LBC; 5 straight months casualties > recruitment — LBC April 18; Putin mediation offer rebuffed by Trump — multiple sources; Cheboksary deep-strike May 5 (Flamingo missiles >1,500 km on VNIIR-Progress C4ISR feedstock) — ISW + Atlantic Council; Ukraine interceptor production ~40K Jan 2026; $50B annual scale — Security Distillery + Reuters convergent.

- **[T3]{.tier .tier-3} inference from evidence:** 201 Ukrainian specialists deployed across 5 Gulf states (single-sourced; Haavik / Security Distillery April 20); 10-year defense cooperation frameworks Saudi/Qatar/UAE (single-sourced; Haavik / Security Distillery April 20); Russia is non-revolutionary petrostate ([Colgan classification]{.gloss data-gloss="colgan-petrostate"}); [Goemans gamble-for-resurrection]{.gloss data-gloss="goemans-gamble-resurrection"} applies to modern Russia (inference); "time favors Ukraine" on 12-month horizon (inference from τ-asymmetric-trajectory); [Mearsheimer multi-front constraint]{.gloss data-gloss="mearsheimer-attrition"} applies to ongoing-war Russia (Posen 1984 closer fit); CRINK currently loose-coupling despite May 2 datum ([Pressman alliance-restraint]{.gloss data-gloss="pressman-alliance-restraint"} inference).

- **[T4]{.tier .tier-4} conjecture:** none in the load-bearing path; "genuinely indeterminate / hybrid" 15% headline alternative is a tier-4 catch-all.

**Six load-bearing T3 inferences** trigger the META rule 5 posterior cap at ≤ 0.45 on the principled-multi-framework headline. The reconciled posterior sits exactly at that cap.

## Pre-mortem {#pre-mortem}

The most likely ways the analysis will be wrong:

1. **[Goemans]{.gloss data-gloss="goemans-gamble-resurrection"} gamble-for-resurrection turns out wrong on Putin** (P ≈ 0.20-0.25). Putin accepts a substantial settlement at next round of negotiations, validating Reiter/Fearon over Goemans. Pre-mortem signal: Putin's acceptance of any settlement reducing pre-war Russian territorial demands by >50% within 12 months.

2. **CRINK financial architecture extends to Russia-buyers within 12 months** (P ≈ 0.30). γ' triggers; Russia gains structural sanctions protection; Steel-man B strengthens. Pre-mortem signal: CRINK extension by end-Q3 2026.

3. **Western support to Ukraine cuts >50% within 12 months** (P ≈ 0.20-0.25). Trump-2 withdraws Ukraine support beyond current pause-and-resume pattern; τ-economic-coalition active side fails. Pre-mortem signal: explicit US weapons-supply termination; EU defense-spending stall; Patriot-supply cessation.

4. **Oil prices sustained >$80/bbl 12+ months** (P ≈ 0.20). Russia's passive gains do not decay; Putin gets sustained budget support; gamble-for-resurrection becomes affordable; trajectory shifts toward Russia-net-winner. Pre-mortem signal: post-Iran-war oil-price stabilization above $80.

5. **Mearsheimer attribution stretch matters more than expected**. The multi-front constraint may not actually hold for ongoing-war Russia in the way the Mearsheimer 1983 framework suggests. Russia's force-generation could recover faster than Ukrainian deep-strike degrades it. Pre-mortem signal: Russian glide-bomb/missile output sustains current acceleration without depletion.

6. **Putin's regime collapses or major elite defection** (P ≈ 0.05). Unforeseen internal-Russia dynamic. Pre-mortem signal: senior elite resignation, Moscow protests, security-service split.

**Lowest-confidence claim**: that the "passive vs active gains" framing (Haavik / Security Distillery) is theoretically rigorous rather than rhetorically attractive. The DA Critique 4 caveat is real — π is descriptively powerful but theoretically grounded only by collapse into Drezner + Ross + Colgan + Pape-inverted formal mechanisms. The framing is defensible as a *useful descriptive integration* of the formal frameworks rather than as an independent theoretical primitive.

**Time-horizon caveat**: the analysis is explicitly limited to 12-month forecast horizon. On longer horizons, Western-support-fragility reverses-on-one-election makes structural claims fragile. The dimension-specific finding may not survive a 2029 US presidential transition that significantly alters Ukraine support.
